# `silk/platform/windows/input`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Raw-byte reads from the Windows standard-input handle.

## When to use
`OsStandardInput` uses [`WindowsInput.read`](#WindowsInput.impl.read) beneath the portable `StandardInput` service.
Console reads use the active console input code page. Redirected files and pipes preserve bytes.

Import as `WindowsInput` with `import silk.platform.windows.input { WindowsInput }`.

<a id="WindowsInput.impl.read"></a>

### Associated function `read`

```silk
pub effect fn read(buffer: &mut [u8], count: &mut usize, error: &mut i32) -> bool
```

Reads once into the buffer and returns success, capturing a Win32 error on failure.

#### Details

Empty buffers make no host call. Each other read resolves the current standard handle and
requests at most 4,294,967,295 bytes. Successful zero-byte reads and broken pipes report
zero bytes with no error, including `ERROR_HANDLE_EOF`. A message-pipe partial read reports its received prefix. The
count is zero on failure, and error is zero for an invalid host count. The handle is never
closed. Console bytes use the active input code page; no text decoding is performed.
